headline: Homelessness pilot program approved, using reallocated budget money and opioid settlement funds.
summary: The plan adds one new position for the rest of FY27, paid from the $25,000 set aside for homelessness program planning. Any other costs would come from opioid settlement funds, and costs after FY27 would go through the regular budget process. Council also passed an emergency change to the parks ordinance that lists 17 Green Street as part of Cannon Plaza park property. It also approved a three-year airport hangar lease with Rampside Aviation, with rent of $800 a month rising to $1,300.
decisions: Approved the appointment of Lori Smith as city manager, unanimously.
Approved appointing Paul Matthews and Kate Snow to the Public Art Commission, unanimously.
Approved moving the Project Canopy Committee into the Sustainability Commission, unanimously; it needs a second reading.
Approved the homelessness pilot program, unanimously.
Approved the Cannon Plaza parks ordinance change on an emergency basis for public safety, unanimously.
Approved the amendment to the rules of the council, unanimously.
Approved moving City Council standing committees into Division 19, unanimously; it needs a second reading.
discussion: Homelessness pilot program funding: Council asked how the program would be funded after FY27 and how often staff would report back. Staff said costs after FY27 would go through the regular budget cycle, and a public speaker said downtown needs more support.

Biddeford Housing Authority TIF amendment: The economic development director proposed capping annual payments to the authority at $68,791 and capturing all new tax revenue at Adam's Point in the TIF. His projections showed about $785,000 for a city TIF account over 30 years, with a public hearing planned at the next council meeting on the 17th.

Community development block grant plan: The program year 2026 plan totals $954,211 and is flexible if priorities change. A 30-day public comment period runs from Tuesday, November 10th through December 14th, with a public hearing on December 15th.

Cannon Plaza emergency change: Staff said city property at 17 Green Street is hard to enforce now, with camping and dumping there. Staff said debris was on the benches behind the Duke Trumbull monument, and the change was passed on public safety grounds.
Project Canopy Committee merger: Staff said state funding for the committee was cut in fiscal year 24. A public speaker said dead trees and stumps remain on Main Street while new trees are planted.
